Hidenori Kusaka: Hidenori Kusaka writes Pokémon Adventures, the long-running manga that follows trainers through every generation of the games, drawn by Mato and later Satoshi Yamamoto.
Gosho Aoyama: Gosho Aoyama created Case Closed (Detective Conan), the mystery series running since 1994, and the earlier adventure comedy Yaiba.
Reki Kawahara: Reki Kawahara writes the light novel series Sword Art Online and Accel World, which launched a wave of virtual-reality game stories and both became hit anime.
Takehiko Inoue: Takehiko Inoue created the basketball classic Slam Dunk, the wheelchair-basketball drama Real, and Vagabond, his stunning retelling of swordsman Miyamoto Musashi's life.
Kazuma Kamachi: Kazuma Kamachi writes the A Certain Magical Index light novels and their spin-offs, including A Certain Scientific Railgun and A Certain Scientific Accelerator.
Akira Toriyama: Akira Toriyama (1955-2024) created Dr. Slump and Dragon Ball, one of the most influential manga ever, and designed the characters for the Dragon Quest games.
Kenjiro Hata: Kenjiro Hata created the parody-packed comedy Hayate the Combat Butler and the sweet newlywed romance Fly Me to the Moon.
Kazuki Takahashi: Kazuki Takahashi (1961-2022) created Yu-Gi-Oh!, whose card game became one of the best-selling trading card games in the world and spawned many spin-off series.
Shinobu Ohtaka: Shinobu Ohtaka created Magi: The Labyrinth of Magic, an Arabian Nights-inspired adventure, along with Sumomomo, Momomo and Orient.
Shinkoshoto: Shinkoshoto writes isekai fantasy light novels including The Strongest Sage with the Weakest Crest, Slow Life in Another World and My Isekai Life.
Ryohgo Narita: Ryohgo Narita writes fast-paced ensemble stories like Baccano! and Durarara!!, set among gangsters, immortals, urban legends and Ikebukuro misfits.
Natsume Akatsuki: Natsume Akatsuki writes the fantasy comedy Konosuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World! and Combatants Will Be Dispatched!.
Fuse: Fuse writes That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime, the isekai hit about a man reborn as a slime who builds a nation of monsters.
Rifujin na Magonote: Rifujin na Magonote writes Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation, one of the stories that shaped the modern isekai genre.
Aneko Yusagi: Aneko Yusagi writes The Rising of the Shield Hero, the isekai fantasy about a hero who is betrayed and must rebuild his name.
Kosuke Fujishima: Kosuke Fujishima created Oh My Goddess!, the long-running romantic comedy about a college student and a goddess, plus You're Under Arrest! and Toppu GP.
coolkyousinnjya: coolkyousinnjya created Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid, the comedy about an office worker whose dragon friend becomes her maid, and Peach Boy Riverside's art.
Izumi Tsubaki: Izumi Tsubaki created the shojo comedies Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun and Oresama Teacher, known for sharp, silly humor.
Kaori Yuki: Kaori Yuki is known for dark, gothic shojo such as Angel Sanctuary, Godchild, Fairy Cube and Grand Guignol Orchestra.
Isuna Hasekura: Isuna Hasekura writes Spice and Wolf, the beloved story of a traveling merchant and a wolf goddess that mixes economics with romance, and its sequel Wolf and Parchment.
FUNA: FUNA writes lighthearted isekai stories including Didn't I Say to Make My Abilities Average in the Next Life?!, Saving 80,000 Gold in Another World for My Retirement and I Shall Survive Using Potions!.
ONE: ONE is the creator of One-Punch Man (redrawn by Yusuke Murata) and Mob Psycho 100. His simple art hides sharp comedy and big hearts.
Yoshiki Nakamura: Yoshiki Nakamura created Skip Beat!, the long-running shojo story about a girl who enters show business to get revenge on her ex.
Osamu Tezuka: Osamu Tezuka (1928-1989), the 'God of Manga', created Astro Boy, Black Jack, Phoenix, Buddha and hundreds more works that shaped manga and anime.
Nobuyuki Anzai: Nobuyuki Anzai created the action series Flame of Recca and the fantasy adventure MÄR.
Reiji Miyajima: Reiji Miyajima created the romantic comedies Rent-A-Girlfriend and The Shiunji Family Children.
Riichiro Inagaki: Riichiro Inagaki wrote the football manga Eyeshield 21 and Dr. Stone, and writes Trillion Game.
Satoshi Wagahara: Satoshi Wagahara writes The Devil Is a Part-Timer!, the comedy about a demon lord working at a fast-food restaurant in Tokyo.
Nagaru Tanigawa: Nagaru Tanigawa writes the Haruhi Suzumiya light novels, about a high school girl who doesn't know she can reshape the world.
Patora Fuyuhara: Patora Fuyuhara writes In Another World with My Smartphone, about a boy reborn in a fantasy world with his phone still working.
Hiroaki Samura: Hiroaki Samura created Blade of the Immortal, the brutal and beautifully drawn samurai epic about a swordsman who cannot die.
Naoki Urasawa: Naoki Urasawa is a master of suspense known for Monster, 20th Century Boys, Pluto, Master Keaton and Asadora!.
Kisetsu Morita: Kisetsu Morita writes cozy fantasy light novels like I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level and I Was a Bottom-Tier Bureaucrat for 1,500 Years.
Tappei Nagatsuki: Tappei Nagatsuki writes Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, the dark isekai about a boy who returns from death to try again.
Kyousuke Motomi: Kyousuke Motomi created the shojo series Dengeki Daisy, Beast Master and QQ Sweeper / Queen's Quality.
Ryo Shirakome: Ryo Shirakome writes Arifureta: From Commonplace to World's Strongest, the action isekai about a weak boy who claws his way to the top.
Kumo Kagyu: Kumo Kagyu writes Goblin Slayer, the dark fantasy about an adventurer who hunts only goblins, and its side stories.
Io Sakisaka: Io Sakisaka creates heartfelt school romances: Strobe Edge, Blue Spring Ride (Ao Haru Ride) and Love Me, Love Me Not.
Kyo Shirodaira: Kyo Shirodaira writes clever mysteries such as Spiral: The Bonds of Reasoning, The Record of a Fallen Vampire and In/Spectre.
Kentaro Miura: Kentaro Miura (1966-2021) created Berserk, the legendary dark fantasy famous for its incredibly detailed art. The series continues with his friend Kouji Mori.
Nozomu Tamaki: Nozomu Tamaki created Dance in the Vampire Bund, about a vampire queen who opens a vampire homeland off the coast of Tokyo.
Mitsutoshi Shimabukuro: Mitsutoshi Shimabukuro created Toriko, the action series about a gourmet hunter tracking down the world's most delicious foods.
Rei Toma: Rei Toma creates fantasy romances such as Dawn of the Arcana, The Water Dragon's Bride and The King's Beast.
Takeshi Konomi: Takeshi Konomi created The Prince of Tennis, the hugely popular sports manga about a young tennis prodigy.
Yuu Tanaka: Yuu Tanaka writes Reincarnated as a Sword, about a man reborn as a magic sword who teams up with a cat-girl.
Ema Toyama: Ema Toyama creates shojo series like Missions of Love, Pixie Pop, I Am Here! and Vampire Dormitory.
Aya Kanno: Aya Kanno created Otomen, about a tough boy who secretly loves girly things, and the dark historical Requiem of the Rose King.
Takaya Kagami: Takaya Kagami writes Seraph of the End and its prequel novels about humanity's fight against vampires.
Makoto Raiku: Makoto Raiku created Zatch Bell! (Konjiki no Gash!!) and the fantasy Animal Land.
Fumi Yoshinaga: Fumi Yoshinaga is known for Ôoku: The Inner Chambers, Antique Bakery, What Did You Eat Yesterday? and many BL works.
Yuto Tsukuda: Yuto Tsukuda wrote Food Wars!: Shokugeki no Soma, the cooking battle series drawn by Shun Saeki.
Hiroya Oku: Hiroya Oku created the intense sci-fi series Gantz, Inuyashiki and Gigant.
Natsumi Ando: Natsumi Ando drew Kitchen Princess and created Arisa, Zodiac P.I. and Something's Wrong with Us.
Muneyuki Kaneshiro: Muneyuki Kaneshiro writes Blue Lock, the soccer survival series drawn by Yusuke Nomura.
Yuki Tabata: Yuki Tabata created Black Clover, the magic fantasy about a boy born without magic who dreams of becoming the Wizard King.
Yoko Kamio: Yoko Kamio created Boys Over Flowers (Hana Yori Dango), one of the best-selling shojo manga ever, adapted into dramas across Asia.
Shuichi Shigeno: Shuichi Shigeno created Initial D, the street-racing manga that made the AE86 and drifting famous worldwide.
Mika Yamamori: Mika Yamamori creates shojo romances like Daytime Shooting Star, Tsubaki-chou Lonely Planet and In the Clear Moonlit Dusk.
Yukiya Murasaki: Yukiya Murasaki writes How NOT to Summon a Demon Lord, the comedic isekai about a gamer pulled into his favorite game as its demon lord.
Wataru Watari: Wataru Watari writes My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected (Oregairu), the sharp-tongued school comedy-drama.
Jun Mochizuki: Jun Mochizuki created the gothic fantasies Pandora Hearts and The Case Study of Vanitas, known for their elegant art.
Gakuto Mikumo: Gakuto Mikumo writes Strike the Blood, about a high schooler who becomes the world's most powerful vampire.
Akimine Kamijyo: Akimine Kamijyo created the samurai action series Samurai Deeper Kyo and Code:Breaker.
Kazune Kawahara: Kazune Kawahara created the shojo comedy High School Debut and wrote My Love Story!!, drawn by Aruko.
Paru Itagaki: Paru Itagaki created Beastars, the drama about a wolf at a school for herbivores and carnivores, plus Beast Complex and Sanda.
Aya Shouoto: Aya Shouoto creates supernatural shojo romances like Kiss of the Rose Princess and The Demon Prince of Momochi House.
Tsutomu Nihei: Tsutomu Nihei, a former architecture student, creates vast sci-fi worlds in Blame!, Knights of Sidonia and Aposimz.
Okina Baba: Okina Baba writes So I'm a Spider, So What?, about a girl reborn as a spider monster in a dungeon.
Yomi Hirasaka: Yomi Hirasaka writes the comedies Haganai: I Don't Have Many Friends and A Sister's All You Need.
Homura Kawamoto: Homura Kawamoto writes Kakegurui: Compulsive Gambler, drawn by Toru Naomura, set at a school ruled by high-stakes gambling.
Kugane Maruyama: Kugane Maruyama writes Overlord, about a gamer trapped in a fantasy world as his undead sorcerer character.
Yellow Tanabe: Yellow Tanabe created Kekkaishi, the supernatural action series about young barrier masters protecting a school at night.
Kenji Saito: Kenji Saito writes Trinity Seven, the magic academy action-comedy drawn by Akinari Nao.
Tomoko Hayakawa: Tomoko Hayakawa created The Wallflower (Yamato Nadeshiko Shichihenge), the comedy about a horror-loving girl and four handsome boys.
Yoshiaki Sukeno: Yoshiaki Sukeno created Twin Star Exorcists and the earlier Binbougami ga!.
Nisio Isin: Nisio Isin is the prolific author of the Monogatari novels, Katanagatari, Juni Taisen: Zodiac War and the Medaka Box manga.
Maki Minami: Maki Minami created the shojo comedies S.A: Special A, Voice Over!: Seiyu Academy and Komomo Confiserie.
Tetsuya Tashiro: Tetsuya Tashiro drew Akame ga Kill! (written by Takahiro) and Slasher Maidens.
Ai Yazawa: Ai Yazawa created the fashion-filled classics Paradise Kiss, Neighborhood Story and the beloved drama Nana.
Yuyuko Takemiya: Yuyuko Takemiya writes the romantic comedies Toradora! and Golden Time.
Taeko Watanabe: Taeko Watanabe created Kaze Hikaru, the long-running historical shojo about a girl who disguises herself to join the Shinsengumi.
Kumanano: Kumanano writes Kuma Kuma Kuma Bear, the cozy isekai about a girl who adventures in an overpowered bear suit.
Naoko Takeuchi: Naoko Takeuchi created Sailor Moon and its prequel Codename: Sailor V, which defined the magical girl genre for a generation.
Ryuto: Ryuto writes the sci-fi isekai Reborn as a Space Mercenary and Survival in Another World with My Mistress!.
singNsong: singNsong (Sing Shong) is the writing duo behind the Korean web novels Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint and The World After the Fall.
Karuho Shiina: Karuho Shiina created Kimi ni Todoke: From Me to You, the gentle shojo romance about a shy girl who is misunderstood by her classmates.
Roy: Roy writes By the Grace of the Gods, the slow-life isekai about a man reborn as a boy who befriends slimes.
Mayu Shinjo: Mayu Shinjo creates steamy shojo romance like Sensual Phrase, Ai Ore! and Demon Love Spell.
Naoshi Arakawa: Naoshi Arakawa created Your Lie in April, the emotional story of a piano prodigy, and Sayonara, Football.
Yuu Kamiya: Yuu Kamiya writes the light novel No Game No Life and co-created Clockwork Planet.
Tohru Fujisawa: Tohru Fujisawa created GTO: Great Teacher Onizuka, its prequel Shonan Junai Gumi, and Rose Hip Rose.
Lynn Okamoto: Lynn Okamoto created the violent sci-fi tragedy Elfen Lied, Brynhildr in the Darkness and Parallel Paradise.
Kentaro Sato: Kentaro Sato creates dark magical girl horror: Magical Girl Site and Magical Girl Apocalypse.
Haro Aso: Haro Aso created the survival thriller Alice in Borderland and writes Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead.
Yuki Midorikawa: Yuki Midorikawa created Natsume's Book of Friends, the gentle, bittersweet series about a boy who can see yokai.
Yukiru Sugisaki: Yukiru Sugisaki created the phantom-thief fantasy D.N.Angel, plus The Candidate for Goddess and Lagoon Engine.
Satoru Noda: Satoru Noda created Golden Kamuy, the action-adventure about a war veteran and an Ainu girl hunting for hidden gold in Hokkaido.
Kia Asamiya: Kia Asamiya created Silent Möbius, Steam Detectives and Dark Angel, and drew a Batman manga.
Mo Xiang Tong Xiu: Mo Xiang Tong Xiu is the Chinese web novelist behind Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation, Heaven Official's Blessing and The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System.
Ryusen Hirotsugu: Ryusen Hirotsugu writes She Professed Herself Pupil of the Wise Man, about a player who logs into a fantasy world as a little girl.
Ryukishi07: Ryukishi07 created the visual novel mysteries Higurashi When They Cry and Umineko When They Cry.
Masakazu Katsura: Masakazu Katsura created the romances Video Girl Ai and I"s, and the superhero series Zetman.
Maybe: Maybe is the creator of To the Abandoned Sacred Beasts and Tales of Wedding Rings.
Yuki Shiwasu: Yuki Shiwasu created the age-gap rom-com Takane & Hana and Tamon's B-Side.
Syougo Kinugasa: Syougo Kinugasa writes Classroom of the Elite, the psychological school drama set at a school where students compete for points.
Shouji Sato: Shouji Sato drew Highschool of the Dead and created Triage X.
Kagiji Kumanomata: Kagiji Kumanomata created Sleepy Princess in the Demon Castle, the comedy about a kidnapped princess who only wants a good night's sleep.
Chika Tojo: Chika Tojo draws the manga adaptation of The Saga of Tanya the Evil, based on Carlo Zen's novels.
Katsura Hoshino: Katsura Hoshino created D.Gray-man, the gothic action series about an exorcist fighting akuma in a 19th-century-inspired world.
Masamune Shirow: Masamune Shirow created Ghost in the Shell, Appleseed and Dominion, landmark cyberpunk manga.
Yuji Iwahara: Yuji Iwahara created King of Thorn, Dimension W and Cat Paradise.
